intent: Practise counting back on the number line where each hop is a move, starting the count on the next number (e.g. 12 - 3, moving back 1 hop to 11, 2 hops to 10, 3 hops to 9).

data.title: Hop Back on the Number Line
data.description: Learn how to subtract numbers within 20 by hopping backward on the number line.

challenges.instruction: Place your finger on 15, and hop backward 5 spaces to find your new spot!
challenges.hint: Count the 5 hop marks carefully as you move your finger to the left.

challenges.instruction: Put your frog at the number 20. Hop back 5 spaces to the left to see where you land!
challenges.hint: Count the hops one by one as you jump backward 5 times.

challenges.instruction: Put your finger on 14. Now, hop backward 4 spaces to the left to see where you land!
challenges.hint: Count each hop carefully as you move 4 steps to the left.

challenges.instruction: Our little frog friend is standing at 8. Help him make 1 hop to the left!
challenges.hint: Count the single hop as the frog jumps backward on the number line.

judgement.reasoning: The detour uses the exact same activity format (number-line) as the current activity without altering the representation. While showing jump arcs emphasizes hops/spaces, the prompt instructions and numbers (e.g. 15-5, 20-5) are not significantly simpler than 12-3, nor do they explicitly address or isolate the misconception of including the starting number in the count.
judgement.verdict: A teacher would likely not use this detour because it repeats the same number-line task without isolating the fencepost error or offering a concrete step-by-step movement representation.
